sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Do you remember airplane travel?
sentences.zh: 你还记得坐飞机旅行的感觉吗？

sentences.en: Packing into a tin can with 200 other people all breathing each other's air?
sentences.zh: 和另外200人挤在一个锡罐里，呼吸着彼此的空气？

sentences.en: Well, these days, most of us are still avoiding planes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如今大多数人仍然在避免坐飞机。

sentences.en: But in the before times, when we boarded a flight,
sentences.zh: 但在过去的那些日子里，当我们登上一架航班时，

sentences.en: we all received the same familiar set of instructions.
sentences.zh: 我们都会收到同样一组熟悉的指令。

sentences.en: For everyone's safety, now would be a good time to review the safety information card,
sentences.zh: 为了大家的安全，现在是阅读安全信息卡的好时机，

sentences.en: which is in your seat pocket.
sentences.zh: 它就在你座位的口袋里。

sentences.en: If you've ever flown on a plane, you've been directed to study the plane's safety briefing card.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐过飞机，你一定被指导过要研究飞机的安全须知卡。

sentences.en: Every passenger plane, commercial or private, has to have safety cards on board.
sentences.zh: 每一架商用或民用客机上都必须备有安全卡。

sentences.en: And if you're like most people, you probably never bothered to examine it too closely.
sentences.zh: 如果你跟大多数人一样，你大概从来没有费心去仔细查看过它。

sentences.en: That is, if you've even looked at it at all.
sentences.zh: 也就是，如果你甚至看都没看过的话。

sentences.en: I always look at these things.
sentences.zh: 我总是看这些东西。

sentences.en: As soon as I sit down on a plane, I pull out the safety card.
sentences.zh: 一坐上飞机，我就会把安全卡抽出来。

sentences.en: Today, I'm going to be talking with producer Mo Laborde
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与制作人莫·拉博德一起探讨

sentences.en: about why safety cards might be worth a closer look.
sentences.zh: 为什么安全卡可能值得我们更仔细地看一看。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗曼。

sentences.en: Hi, Mo.
sentences.zh: 嗨，莫。

sentences.en: So you're saying you always pull out the safety card?
sentences.zh: 所以你是说你总是会把安全卡抽出来？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, what can I say?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我能说什么呢？

sentences.en: I just love airplane safety cards.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢飞机安全卡。

sentences.en: Honestly, I think I love them like a little bit too much.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我觉得我喜欢得有点儿过头了。

sentences.en: I don't just look at them.
sentences.zh: 我不只是看看它们。

sentences.en: I collect them.
sentences.zh: 我在收集它们。

sentences.en: I've been collecting for about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我已经收集大约10年了。

sentences.en: 10 years.
So when you say you collect them, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 所以当你说你收集它们时，是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, whenever I fly on the plane,
sentences.zh: 嗯，每当我坐飞机时，

sentences.en: I just snag the card and I put it in my backpack.
sentences.zh: 我就会顺走安全卡，然后把它放进我的双肩包里。

sentences.en: So you just take them.
sentences.zh: 所以你只是把它们拿走了。

sentences.en: Is that allowed?
sentences.zh: 这被允许吗？

sentences.en: I'd actually don't know.
sentences.zh: 其实我不知道。

sentences.en: Is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 这算是个问题吗？

sentences.en: It's a good question because it's technically not allowed,
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题，因为严格来说这是不允许的，

sentences.en: but I just have such a strong kleptomania for this one object.
sentences.zh: 但我对这个单一的物品有着如此强烈的偷窃癖。

sentences.en: Today in my collection, I have about 300.
sentences.zh: 今天在我的收藏中，我有大约300张。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: So why do you have 300 safety cards?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么会有300张安全卡？

sentences.en: I think it's that for me, I fell in love with them because they're like safety themed comic strips.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，我爱上它们是因为它们就像安全主题的连环画。

sentences.en: Like the outfits of the women are stuck in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 比如女性的服装还停留在20世纪60年代。

sentences.en: There are little girls wearing Mary Jane shoes and bobby socks.
sentences.zh: 有穿着玛丽简鞋和泡泡袜的小女孩。

sentences.en: And it's just so, the way they look is so fascinating to me.
sentences.zh: 它们的外观对我有极大的吸引力。

sentences.en: But more than that, like I am especially fascinated with the way that they depict a plane crash.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，我对它们描绘飞机失事的方式尤为着迷。

sentences.en: Like it's this alternate version of events where there's no blood, there's no wreckage from the crash.
sentences.zh: 就像这是一个没有血迹、没有飞机残骸的平行时空版本的事件。

sentences.en: Nobody's distressed.
sentences.zh: 没有人感到痛苦。

sentences.en: And their hair doesn't even get messed up.
sentences.zh: 他们的发型甚至都没有乱。

sentences.en: Like it's so obviously the opposite of what an actual plane crash would look like.
sentences.zh: 这显然与真实空难的场景完全相反。

sentences.en: Like absolutely, when I see these cards, I always think of the movie Fight Club where Brad Pitt's character is just,
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，当我看到这些卡片时，我总是会想起电影《搏击俱乐部》，布拉德·皮特饰演的角色，

sentences.en: just outright mocks the way that people look on these cards.
sentences.zh: 简直是在公开嘲讽人们在这些卡片上的样子。

sentences.en: Emergency water landing, 600 miles an hour.
sentences.zh: 水上紧急迫降，时速600英里。

sentences.en: Blank faces, calm as Hindu cows.
sentences.zh: 面无表情，冷静得像印度神牛。

sentences.en: The illusion of safety.
sentences.zh: 安全的幻觉。

sentences.en: And then like later on, you see Ed Norton and Brad Pitt replace the normal safety cards with cards where everyone is like freaked out and panicking.
sentences.zh: 然后后来，你会看到爱德华·诺顿和布拉德·皮特用一张张每个人都吓坏了、惊慌失措的卡片替换了正常的安全卡。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that the Fight Club scene gets at something about how most of us think the cards aren't actually necessary.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为《搏击俱乐部》的那个场景触及了我们大多数人认为这些卡片其实并不必要的原因。

sentences.en: Like at some gut level, we just assume that if we're in a crash, everyone's going to die.
sentences.zh: 就像在某种直觉层面，我们只是假设如果我们遭遇坠机，每个人都会死。

sentences.en: But then after I began collecting them, I started looking into the history of these cards and where they come from.
sentences.zh: 但后来在我开始收集它们之后，我开始研究这些卡片的历史以及它们的来源。

sentences.en: And basically what I learned is that we have that all wrong.
sentences.zh: 基本上我了解到的是，我们完全想错了。

sentences.en: Safety cards work.
sentences.zh: 安全卡是有用的。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I would not have thought that.
sentences.zh: 我可不会这么想。

sentences.en: Yeah, reading a safety card can save your life.
sentences.zh: 是的，阅读安全卡可以救你的命。

sentences.en: But also it turns out that safety cards have played a central role in our evolving understanding of how to survive a plane crash.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，安全卡在我们对如何从空难中幸存这一认识的演变过程中发挥了核心作用。

sentences.en: All right, well tell me more.
sentences.zh: 好吧，跟我多讲讲。

sentences.en: What is it that we owe to the safety card?
sentences.zh: 我们究竟该感谢安全卡什么？

sentences.en: Well, to answer that, first, we have to go back a ways to a time when safety cards were pretty much useless.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了回答这个问题，首先我们要追溯到安全卡几乎毫无用处的时代。

sentences.en: In fact, they weren't even really about safety.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们甚至真的与安全无关。

sentences.en: Because in the early days of passenger airplane travel in the 1930s, there was no regulation at all about what should go in the cards.
sentences.zh: 因为在20世纪30年代客运飞机旅行的早期，对于卡片上应该写什么没有任何规定。

sentences.en: And in the beginning, airlines had to convince people to get on planes because people were scared to fly.
sentences.zh: 起初，航空公司必须说服人们登机，因为人们害怕飞行。

sentences.en: So the early cards were all about soothing passengers, selling them on the idea that air travel was safe and glamorous.
sentences.zh: 所以早期的卡片全都是为了安抚乘客，向他们兜售航空旅行是安全且迷人的理念。

sentences.en: And they were essentially just miniature versions of those travel postcards, like little advertisements for the airlines.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上只是旅游明信片的微缩版，就像航空公司的微型广告一样。

sentences.en: So here, let me show you a really early card.
sentences.zh: 所以，我来给你展示一张非常早期的卡片。

sentences.en: This one was made by Imperial Airways in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 这张是帝国航空公司在20世纪30年代制作的。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: This one says Imperial Airways, comfort and convenience.
sentences.zh: 这张上面写着帝国航空公司，舒适与便利。

sentences.en: And there's little cherubs carrying a fat fancy man in a hammock.
sentences.zh: 上面还有小天使抬着一个胖乎乎、衣着考究的男人躺在吊床里。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 真可爱。

sentences.en: That is not the depiction of air travel in any way, shape or form.
sentences.zh: 这根本就不是任何形式的航空旅行的写照。

sentences.en: No, it's a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 不，这是一个幻想。

sentences.en: And if you open it up, all of the instructions pretty much are, it's all text.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它打开，所有的说明基本上都是文字。

sentences.en: Okay, so here's some of this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里有一些这样的内容。

sentences.en: To inflate the belt, hold the air bottle, which you can feel inside the belt, in the left hand, and press lever B upwards with the right hand.
sentences.zh: 要使救生带充气，请用左手握住可以感觉到在救生带内部的气瓶，然后用右手将B杆向上按。

sentences.en: That is not very clear.
sentences.zh: 这不是很清楚。

sentences.en: Do you know what that means?
sentences.zh: 你知道那是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: No, I really don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我真不知道。

sentences.en: And sadly, this card is characteristic of the whole first wave of safety car design throughout the 30s and 40s.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，这张卡片是整个30和40年代第一波安全卡设计特征的缩影。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And to be fair, by the mid-60s, things had improved a bit.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，到了60年代中期，情况已经有所改善。

sentences.en: You start to see these things called fleet cards,
sentences.zh: 你开始看到被称为机型卡的东西，

sentences.en: which were almost like spiral-bound booklets that contained the safety instructions for multiple plane models in multiple languages.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎就像是螺旋装订的小册子，包含了多种语言的多种飞机型号的安全说明。

sentences.en: But that often just made it harder to find the correct safety information because there were so many pages to flip through.
sentences.zh: 但那往往只是让人更难找到正确的安全信息，因为有太多页需要翻阅。

sentences.en: So how did we get from that to the kinds of cards that we're familiar with today?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是怎么从那种卡片演变成我们今天熟悉的这种卡片的呢？

sentences.en: Well, things really started to change in the late 1960s when airlines started noticing a troubling pattern when it came to crashes.
sentences.zh: 事情在20世纪60年代末真正开始发生变化，当时航空公司开始注意到一个令人不安的规律，当涉及到坠机时。

sentences.en: Impact survival was possible, but not escape.
sentences.zh: 撞击后生还并非不可能，但逃生却很难。

sentences.en: Dan Johnson is a psychologist who specializes in airplane safety.
sentences.zh: 丹·约翰逊是一位专注于飞机安全的心理学家。

sentences.en: And he says that in the 50s and 60s, air travel was growing increasingly safe.
sentences.zh: 他说，在50和60年代，航空旅行变得越来越安全。

sentences.en: Planes crashed less often.
sentences.zh: 飞机坠毁的频率降低了。

sentences.en: And when they did crash, thanks to design improvements, those crashes were less fatal.
sentences.zh: 当它们确实坠毁时，由于设计的改进，这些坠机事故的致命性降低了。

sentences.en: All of which should have added up to more survivors.
sentences.zh: 所有这些本应该带来更多的幸存者。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, those survivors were not always getting out of the airplane in time to survive.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，这些幸存者并不总是能及时逃出飞机以保全性命。

sentences.en: And I have to say, this is the part of the story that made me throw out everything I had assumed about airplane safety.
sentences.zh: 我必须得说，故事的这一部分让我抛弃了我对飞机安全的所有假设。

sentences.en: Because it turns out that if you're in a serious crash, it's not the impact that kills you.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，如果你遭遇了严重的坠机事故，致命的不是撞击本身。

sentences.en: There's very few accidents that kill everyone aboard.
sentences.zh: 极少有事故会杀死机上的所有人。

sentences.en: Instead, what kills you is what happens next.
sentences.zh: 相反，致命的是接下来发生的事情。

sentences.en: It's the smoke and fire inside the cabin after the crash.
sentences.zh: 那是坠机后机舱内的浓烟和烈火。

sentences.en: So the key to surviving is getting out of the plane as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以生还的关键是以尽可能快的速度逃离飞机。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: I guess I never thought about it that way before, that the important thing is just exiting the plane.
sentences.zh: 我想我以前从未这样想过，最重要的事情居然只是撤离飞机。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is the realization accident investigators had in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这就是20世纪60年代事故调查人员得出的认识。

sentences.en: They calculated that in your average crash, people had about 90 seconds to get out of the plane before it became, quote unquote, unsurvivable.
sentences.zh: 他们计算出，在一般的坠机事故中，人们大约有90秒的时间逃离飞机，否则飞机就会变得，引号内的，无法生还。

sentences.en: But again and again, they found that passengers weren't making it out in time.
sentences.zh: 但他们一次又一次地发现，乘客并没有及时逃生。

sentences.en: In one accident, for example, there were 101 passengers aboard, four survivors.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一次事故中，机上有101名乘客，有4名幸存者。

sentences.en: And the people who were killed were not killed as a result of the impact, but because they couldn't get out to the door.
sentences.zh: 遇难的人不是因为撞击而死，而是因为他们无法走到门边。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so dreadful.
sentences.zh: 哦，太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's nightmare fuel.
sentences.zh: 这简直是噩梦般的场景。

sentences.en: And it was a nightmare for the airline industry, too.
sentences.zh: 对航空业来说这也是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Which is why, in 1968, Douglas Aircraft decided to improve their safety record by hiring Dan, along with another guy named Bo Altman.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在1968年，道格拉斯飞机公司决定通过聘请丹以及另一个名叫博·奥尔特man的人来改善他们的安全记录。

sentences.en: I had never been on an airplane in my life.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没坐过飞机。

sentences.en: That's Bo.
sentences.zh: 那是博。

sentences.en: Like Dan, he's also a psychologist who specializes in airplane safety.
sentences.zh: 和丹一样，他也是一位专注于飞机安全的心理学家。

sentences.en: But back when he was first hired at Douglas, he says he didn't know the first thing about air travel.
sentences.zh: 但回想他刚被道格拉斯聘用时，他说他对航空旅行一无所知。

sentences.en: Well, I didn't lie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没有撒谎。

sentences.en: But I'd never been on one of those great, big, monster airplanes.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没有坐过那些又大又庞大的飞机。

sentences.en: So the first time he entered a proper passenger plane was to give it a safety inspection.
sentences.zh: 因此，他第一次进入一架真正的客机是为了对其进行安全检查。

sentences.en: And my first inclination was when I entered the back door of the airplane was, where are the exits?
sentences.zh: 我进入飞机后门时的第一反应是，出口在哪里？

sentences.en: And I could not see any exits.
sentences.zh: 我什么出口也看不到。

sentences.en: I could only see the door, which I came through.
sentences.zh: 我只能看到我进来的那扇门。

sentences.en: And I said, well, how does a passenger know where to go in the event of an emergency?
sentences.zh: 我说，那乘客在紧急情况下怎么知道该去哪里？

sentences.en: So he started walking through the airplane and he noticed all the doors were covered with curtains.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始在飞机里走动，发现所有的门都挂着窗帘。

sentences.en: And why were they covered?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们被遮盖起来？

sentences.en: Was it just for aesthetics?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了美观吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: They didn't want anybody to know that there was a possibility of an emergency exit there.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让任何人知道那里有可能是紧急出口。

sentences.en: They didn't want to talk about safety at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不想谈论安全问题。

sentences.en: And then he took a look at their safety cards.
sentences.zh: 然后他看了一下他们的安全卡。

sentences.en: So I looked at it and I said, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以我看了一眼，然后说，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I said, it's all in three languages and no pictures or nothing.
sentences.zh: 我说，全都是三种语言，连图片也没有。

sentences.en: It was just read it and weep.
sentences.zh: 简直是没眼看。

sentences.en: And I said, we've got a problem here.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们这里有个问题。

sentences.en: We need to teach passengers how to get out of that airplane in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 我们需要教乘客如何在紧急情况下逃离那架飞机。

sentences.en: So Bo and Dan decided to found a company together to improve airline safety procedures.
sentences.zh: 于是博和丹决定共同创立一家公司来改善航空安全程序。

sentences.en: They called it the Interaction Research Corporation.
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为互动研究公司。

sentences.en: And their specialty was running tests in mock cabins full of research participants.
sentences.zh: 他们的专长是在充满研究参与者的模拟客舱中进行测试。

sentences.en: So Dan and I did tons of work on how do we get 450 people aboard that airplane off, everybody off, including the crew, in 90 seconds.
sentences.zh: 所以丹和我做了大量的研究，关于如何让450人登上那架飞机，然后所有人，包括机组人员在内，在90秒内全部撤离。

sentences.en: And they would start by making each test as realistic as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们会从使每次测试尽可能逼真开始。

sentences.en: They always made sure that there were X amount of people under the age of six and so many people over the age of 70.
sentences.zh: 他们总是确保有一定数量6岁以下的儿童和一定数量70岁以上的老人。

sentences.en: And they have only been given their passenger briefing that it would be on a regular airplane.
sentences.zh: 他们只得到了这是在一架普通飞机上的乘客简报。

sentences.en: And then they would just toss a smoke bomb into the fake plane cabin.
sentences.zh: 然后他们只需将一枚烟雾弹扔进假飞机的客舱里。

sentences.en: Then, boom, lights go off.
sentences.zh: 然后，轰的一声，灯灭了。

sentences.en: Emergency, emergency, evacuate, evacuate.
sentences.zh: 紧急情况，紧急情况，紧急疏散，紧急疏散。

sentences.en: Release your seatbelt, release your seatbelt.
sentences.zh: 解开安全带，解开安全带。

sentences.en: Get up, get up, get up.
sentences.zh: 起来，起来，起来。

sentences.en: Move, move, move.
sentences.zh: 快动，快动，快动。

sentences.en: Get to the exit.
sentences.zh: 去到出口。

sentences.en: And then when they got to the exit.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们到达出口时。

sentences.en: They would be 15 feet above the ground.
sentences.zh: 他们离地面会有15英尺高。

sentences.en: And they had to jump into an inflatable slide in the dark.
sentences.zh: 他们得在黑暗中跳进充气滑梯里。

sentences.en: And they'd never done it before.
sentences.zh: 而且他们以前从未做过。

sentences.en: In trying to get everyone moving as fast as possible, these experiments could actually get dangerous.
sentences.zh: 为了让每个人尽可能快地行动起来，这些实验实际上可能会变得很危险。

sentences.en: I have no doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah, they got a little out of hand.
sentences.zh: 是啊，它们有点失控了。

sentences.en: We tried to provide as much realism as we could without hurting people.
sentences.zh: 我们试图在不伤害人们的前提下，提供尽可能高的真实感。

sentences.en: We still hurt a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我们还是弄伤了很多人。

sentences.en: Early.
sentences.zh: 早期。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of people got hurt jumping out of the slides.
sentences.zh: 对，很多人在从滑梯上跳下来时受伤了。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, we did it.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，我们还是做了。

sentences.en: It's for the greater good.
sentences.zh: 这是为了更大的利益。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And their tests were an information goldmine.
sentences.zh: 他们的测试简直是信息的金矿。

sentences.en: All the participants would be wearing numbered vests indicating their seat number, their age, their gender.
sentences.zh: 所有参与者都会穿着印有座位号、年龄和性别的编号背心。

sentences.en: And Bo and Dan would be filming the whole thing to see who went where and who did what.
sentences.zh: 博和丹会拍摄整个过程，以观察谁去了哪里，谁做了什么。

sentences.en: I figured that I had looked at about 10,000 people over 10 years looking at whether they sat down at the door sill, how long they waited,
sentences.zh: 我估计在10年里我观察了大约10000人，看他们是否坐在门槛上，他们等待了多久，

sentences.en: did they follow the behavior of the passenger in front?
sentences.zh: 他们会模仿前面乘客的行为吗？

sentences.en: So, for example, with that thing Dan just mentioned, whenever people sat down at the door before going down the slide, they found that it took an extra half second per person.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，正如丹刚才提到的那样，每当人们在滑下滑梯前坐在舱门处时，他们发现每个人会多花半秒钟。

sentences.en: And if you've got maybe 100 passengers going out a door, then that's 40 or 50 seconds.
sentences.zh: 如果你有大约100名乘客从一个门出去，那就是40或50秒。

sentences.en: But if you need to get everyone out in 90 seconds, then 50 seconds is more than you can afford.
sentences.zh: 但如果你需要在90秒内让所有人撤离，那么50秒就是你无法承受的。

sentences.en: So I thought the jumping on the slide was a structural thing, but that's actually just a time thing?
sentences.zh: 所以我以为在滑梯上跳跃是出于结构方面的考虑，但实际上这只是时间问题？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I thought that too, that sitting down would, like, damage the slide.
sentences.zh: 我也这么想，以为坐着会像那样损坏滑梯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: No, it's all about getting the passengers out as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 不，这完全是为了以最快速度让乘客撤离。

sentences.en: Oh, that is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 哦，太迷人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But one of the most important things Bo and Dan learned was that one of the best ways to get out of the airplane on time was, surprise, to read the safety card.
sentences.zh: 但博和丹学到的最重要的事情之一就是，按时撤离飞机的最佳方法之一，不出所料，是阅读安全须知卡。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: They're important.
sentences.zh: 它们很重要。

sentences.en: They really are important.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很重要。

sentences.en: When they had people read the safety cards and when those cards had the relevant information, the evacuation times improved dramatically.
sentences.zh: 当他们让人们阅读安全须知卡，并且当这些卡片包含相关信息时，疏散时间得到了显著改善。

sentences.en: So they began applying what they learned in the experiments to the design of the cards.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始将从实验中学到的知识应用到卡片的设计中。

sentences.en: And we said, OK, how can we improve these?
sentences.zh: 我们当时说，好吧，我们该如何改进这些？

sentences.en: And then we said, no words, just pictures.
sentences.zh: 然后我们说，不要文字，只要图片。

sentences.en: And then Bo and Dan would test the cards out on the public and see if people could understand the illustration.
sentences.zh: 接着，博和丹会向公众测试这些卡片，看看人们是否能理解图解。

sentences.en: We'd say, have you got a second here, mister?
sentences.zh: 我们会说，先生，能耽误你一秒钟吗？

sentences.en: We've got something here we'd like for you to take a look at and tell us what you think.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有些东西想请你看看，并告诉我们你的想法。

sentences.en: And we have to have 90 percent understandability or we're not going to sell this card.
sentences.zh: 我们必须达到百分之九十的理解度，否则我们是不会推行这张卡片的。

sentences.en: And the result was cards that look a lot like the cards you see today.
sentences.zh: 结果就是这些卡片看起来很像你今天看到的卡片。

sentences.en: They used pictures to tell the entire story of how to exit the plane.
sentences.zh: 他们用图片讲述了如何离开飞机的完整过程。

sentences.en: And they zoomed in on specific important actions like how to open a door.
sentences.zh: 他们放大了特定的重要动作，比如如何打开机门。

sentences.en: And there were also things that you might not consciously notice, but which apparently really help,
sentences.zh: 还有一些你可能不会有意识注意到，但显然确实很有帮助的事情，

sentences.en: like using red for all the exit-related arrows and pretty much having no text on the card except for the word exit.
sentences.zh: 比如所有与出口相关的箭头都使用红色，并且卡片上除了“出口”这个词之外几乎没有其他文字。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I've never really thought about that, but exit is the only word.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有真正想过这一点，但“出口”是唯一的词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They just contained all these visual strategies that nudge the reader towards comprehension.
sentences.zh: 它们只包含所有这些能促使读者去理解的视觉策略。

sentences.en: And as a final little design flourish, instead of like getting swallowed up by the seat back pocket, their cards actually fit.
sentences.zh: 作为一个最后的微小设计巧思，他们的卡片并没有像被座椅背后的口袋吞没那样，而是非常合身。

sentences.en: So the title would just peek out and sort of entice the passenger to open it up.
sentences.zh: 所以标题会微微露出，以此诱导乘客将其打开。

sentences.en: And when they looked down, all they could see was just in case.
sentences.zh: 当他们向下看时，他们能看到的只有“以防万一”。

sentences.en: Intriguing.
sentences.zh: 耐人寻味。

sentences.en: Just in case.
sentences.zh: 以防万一。

sentences.en: Just in case what?
sentences.zh: 以防万一什么？

sentences.en: This is the ABC Evening News with Harry Reisner and Barbara Walters.
sentences.zh: 这里是ABC晚间新闻，我是哈里·赖斯纳和芭芭拉·沃尔特斯。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: Yesterday, the averages caught up with a 747.
sentences.zh: 昨天，平均数据终于在一个波音747身上应验了。

sentences.en: Two of them, both on charter flights, both on the ground, collided at Tenerife Airport in the Canary Islands.
sentences.zh: 两架747，都是包机，都在地面上，在加那利群岛的特内里费机场相撞了。

sentences.en: The Tenerife crash in March of 1977 is the moment where Bo and Dan's cards really were put to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 1977年3月的特内里费空难是博和丹的安全卡真正接受考验的时刻。

sentences.en: Because it involved two large planes, it's still the single deadliest aviation accident in history.
sentences.zh: 由于涉及两架大型飞机，它仍然是历史上造成死亡人数最多的单起航空事故。

sentences.en: Why it happened is kind of up for debate.
sentences.zh: 它为什么会发生尚存争议。

sentences.en: But basically, a 747 belonging to KLM, an airline carrier, collided on takeoff with a Pan Am 747 that was still on the runway.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，一架属于荷兰皇家航空公司的747客机在起飞时，与一架仍在跑道上的泛美航空747客机相撞。

sentences.en: And the KLM plane tore the roof off of the Pan Am plane.
sentences.zh: 荷兰皇家航空公司的飞机削掉了泛美飞机机顶。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 我的天呐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And on the KLM plane, everyone died.
sentences.zh: 荷兰皇家航空公司的飞机上，所有人都遇难了。

sentences.en: And that easily could have been the case with the Pan Am plane, too.
sentences.zh: 泛美航空的飞机也完全有可能遭遇同样的命运。

sentences.en: It got very hot inside the Pan Am plane because of the fuel.
sentences.zh: 由于燃油的原因，泛美飞机内部变得非常热。

sentences.en: Fuel leaking down from the KLM plane into the cabin.
sentences.zh: 燃油从荷兰皇家航空的飞机泄漏到客舱里。

sentences.en: So, at a certain point, the conditions in the cabin became unsurvivable.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时刻，客舱内的环境变得无法生存。

sentences.en: But 67 people did survive.
sentences.zh: 但有67人生还了。

sentences.en: And it turned out that Dan and Bo designed the safety card for the Pan Am 747, meaning their card was the one on board the plane with the survivors.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，丹和博设计了泛美747的安全须知卡，这意味着他们的卡片正是幸存者所乘飞机上的那张。

sentences.en: And one of them, at least, that I talked to said that if it wasn't for the safety card, he and his wife would not have gotten out of the plane.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的其中一位幸存者表示，如果不是因为那张安全卡，他和妻子根本无法逃出飞机。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, apparently this one couple, Paul and Floyd Heck, somewhat famously escaped the crash while clutching a safety card in their hands.
sentences.zh: 对，显然有一对夫妇，保罗和弗洛伊德·赫克，手里紧紧攥着一张安全须知卡，在某种程度上他们因此而闻名地逃过了空难。

sentences.en: And I actually have a copy of that safety card.
sentences.zh: 我其实有一份那张安全卡的复印件。

sentences.en: Okay, so let me check this out.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我来看看这个。

sentences.en: So, it says 747, just in case, dot, dot, dot.
sentences.zh: 上面写着747，以防万一，点，点，点。

sentences.en: And you open it up, and it's really like the modern card, you know, like it has opened up the door, jumping onto the slide, the layout of the plane.
sentences.zh: 你把它打开，它真的很像现代的卡片，你知道的，比如它画了打开机门、跳上滑梯、飞机的布局。

sentences.en: And it is a quantum leap forward over the ones you showed me earlier that were all text, you know, in beautiful pictures, but really just impenetrable.
sentences.zh: 与你之前给我看的那些全是文字、密密麻麻的卡片相比，它实现了飞跃式的发展，你知道的，上面的图片很漂亮，但实际上确实让人难以看懂。

sentences.en: Yeah, it seems like one that would save lives.
sentences.zh: 是的，这看起来是一张能救命的卡片。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they really saw the fact that there were survivors in Tenerife as kind of a vindication of their work.
sentences.zh: 特内里费机场有生还者这一事实，被他们视为对自己工作的某种平反与证明。

sentences.en: And after Tenerife, Bo and Dan actually testified before Congress about the need for better airline safety procedures.
sentences.zh: 特内里费空难之后，博和丹甚至在国会作证，陈述改进航空安全程序的必要性。

sentences.en: And it's around that time that the all-visual safety cards became the standard throughout the industry.
sentences.zh: 也正是在那个时候，全视觉的安全卡成为了整个行业的标准。

sentences.en: So, did they learn anything else from the tragedy at Tenerife?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们从特内里费的悲剧中学到了其他什么吗？

sentences.en: Like, were there things that they discovered that they could have done better, even?
sentences.zh: 比如说，有没有发现他们本可以做得更好的地方？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Given that some of the survivors said the safety cards definitely helped them, why weren't there even more survivors?
sentences.zh: 既然一些幸存者说安全卡确实帮了他们，为什么没有更多的幸存者呢？

sentences.en: And they found that there are really two big hurdles preventing people from absorbing the information in the safety cards.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，阻碍人们吸收安全卡中信息的其实有两个巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: The first is that when the crash happened, a lot of people just froze.
sentences.zh: 首先是当空难发生时，很多人直接呆住了。

sentences.en: Some of the survivors gave us some information on, they were going down the aisleway to get to an exit, and there were people sitting there with their mouth open.
sentences.zh: 一些幸存者向我们提供了一些信息：他们正沿着过道走向出口，而有些人坐在那里，嘴巴张得大大的。

sentences.en: They didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该做什么。

sentences.en: They didn't know what to move.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该移动什么。

sentences.en: They didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没做。

sentences.en: They just sat there and died.
sentences.zh: 他们就坐在那里等死。

sentences.en: Investigators at Tenerife found that some of the victims were still buckled in their seats.
sentences.zh: 特内里费的调查人员发现，一些遇难者仍然系着安全带坐在座位上。

sentences.en: Like, they were so shocked they couldn't even unbuckle their seatbelts.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们受到了极大的惊吓，甚至无法解开安全带。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is pretty creepy.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: But it's also apparently common in plane crashes.
sentences.zh: 但这在空难中显然也很常见。

sentences.en: It's called tonic immobility.
sentences.zh: 这被称为紧张性不动。

sentences.en: And psychologists think that this is like a primitive defense mechanism.
sentences.zh: 心理学家认为这是一种原始的防御机制。

sentences.en: Because one way to get a predator to leave you alone is just to play dead.
sentences.zh: 因为让掠食者对你不理不睬的方法之一就是装死。

sentences.en: And it turns out that this explains the thing that, from the beginning, I have found the most perplexing about the safety cards.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这解释了一件从一开始就让我对安全卡感到最困惑的事情。

sentences.en: Why in the world of the safety card is everything so orderly and sort of panicless?
sentences.zh: 为什么安全卡上的所有东西都那么井然有序，而且似乎毫无恐慌？

sentences.en: I think that there's a fear of being in an airplane accident, and anything that we do that might increase that fear would probably increase the incidence of tonic immobility.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对卷入飞机事故感到恐惧，而我们所做的任何可能增加这种恐惧的行为，都可能会增加紧张性不动症的发生率。

sentences.en: The placid faces.
sentences.zh: 平静的脸庞。

sentences.en: The perfectly coiffed hair.
sentences.zh: 完美的发型。

sentences.en: The very thing that Fight Club is making fun of, it turns out that that is not like a shallow corporate marketing decision.
sentences.zh: 正是《搏击俱乐部》所嘲讽的那些东西，事实证明，那并不是什么肤浅的企业营销决策。

sentences.en: Dan says the bloodless design is at least partially about keeping passengers from panicking even more and maybe even freezing up.
sentences.zh: 丹说，这种波澜不惊的设计至少有一部分是为了防止乘客陷入更严重的恐慌，甚至可能因此吓得呆若木鸡。

sentences.en: So, you mentioned that there are two big hurdles.
sentences.zh: 所以，你提到有两个巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: One is that the people freeze up before using the information on the cards.
sentences.zh: 一个是人们在利用卡片上的信息之前就吓呆了。

sentences.en: What's the second big hurdle when it comes to safety cards?
sentences.zh: 说到安全卡，第二个巨大障碍是什么？

sentences.en: The second hurdle is something that we talked about at the very beginning of the story, which is that nobody reads them.
sentences.zh: 第二个障碍是我们在这个故事一开始就讨论过的内容，那就是根本没人读它们。

sentences.en: Nobody reads the cards.
sentences.zh: 没有人读这些卡片。

sentences.en: Besides you.
sentences.zh: 除了你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It turns out that the little just-in-case teaser doesn't really work that well.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那个小小的“以防万一”的悬念并不怎么管用。

sentences.en: You're going to get a lot of people that says, I am not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 你会遇到很多人说，我才不干呢。

sentences.en: I don't want to read this.
sentences.zh: 我不想读这个。

sentences.en: I don't want to look at it.
sentences.zh: 我不想看它。

sentences.en: I don't want to do anything at all about it, period.
sentences.zh: 关于这事我什么也不想做，句号。

sentences.en: I want to get to Dallas, and I don't give a s**t about anything else.
sentences.zh: 我只想去达拉斯，其他任何事我他妈的一概不在乎。

sentences.en: I mean, that's their attitude.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他们的态度。

sentences.en: Dan told me that even today, only 3 or 4% of passengers ever pick up the safety card.
sentences.zh: 丹告诉我，即使在今天，也只有3%到4%的乘客会拿起安全须知卡。

sentences.en: Is this why they now do safety videos, you know, not relying solely on the cards?
sentences.zh: 这就是他们现在制作安全视频的原因吗，你知道的，不仅仅依赖卡片？

sentences.en: Well, the videos help up to a point, but even the briefing videos have their limits.
sentences.zh: 嗯，视频在一定程度上起到了帮助作用，但即使是简报视频也有其局限性。

sentences.en: Like, they work really well with first-time flyers, but they still fall flat, just like the cards, when it comes to frequent flyers.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们对初次乘机的人非常有效，但一遇到经常坐飞机的常客，它们就和卡片一样行不通了。

sentences.en: So you get the cards and you get the videos, and also things like the flight demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 所以你既有卡片，又有视频，还有像乘务员演示这样的东西。

sentences.en: But I wonder if there's any other way to reach the most resistant passengers.
sentences.zh: 但我在想，有没有什么其他方法能触及那些最排斥的乘客。

sentences.en: Like, have they tried other things to inject the necessary information into people's brains?
sentences.zh: 例如，他们有没有尝试过其他方法把必要的信息灌输到人们的大脑中？

sentences.en: So there are some other methods that airline companies have tried to get passengers' attention, and they haven't gone that well.
sentences.zh: 航空公司确实尝试过其他一些方法来吸引乘客的注意力，但进展得并不顺利。

sentences.en: Bo told me about this one carrier, Eastern Airlines, that tried an experiment.
sentences.zh: 博跟我讲过一家航空公司，美国东方航空，他们曾做过一个实验。

sentences.en: They had everybody to come into the facility 15 minutes early.
sentences.zh: 他们让所有人提前15分钟进入大楼。

sentences.en: And then they had to go to this room, and they got the passenger safety briefing in the room.
sentences.zh: 然后他们必须去这个房间，并在房间里听取乘客安全简报。

sentences.en: Then they went out of business.
sentences.zh: 后来他们倒闭了。

sentences.en: Bo says, the cards, the demonstrations, the videos, they all help get more information across to more people.
sentences.zh: 博说，卡片、演示、视频，它们都有助于向更多人传达更多信息。

sentences.en: But in the end, the information will always hit this wall of resistance among passengers.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这些信息总是会撞上乘客们这堵抗拒之墙。

sentences.en: We try to teach them.
sentences.zh: 我们试图教导他们。

sentences.en: We try to encourage them.
sentences.zh: 我们试图鼓励他们。

sentences.en: We do all those things.
sentences.zh: 我们把这些都做了。

sentences.en: But people's attitudes stick.
sentences.zh: 但人们的观念根深蒂固。

sentences.en: And you can't change that.
sentences.zh: 而你无法改变这一点。

sentences.en: You cannot change that.
sentences.zh: 你无法改变这一点。

sentences.en: So you have to look at it and say, how many people can I trust to do what they're told to do?
sentences.zh: 所以你只能看着并心想，我能信任多少人去照着要求做？

sentences.en: Probably 30%.
But what do you do?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么办呢？

sentences.en: You have to play the odds.
sentences.zh: 你必须孤注一掷去碰运气。

sentences.en: That's all there is to it.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: So really, when it comes down to it, if I really want to survive a crash or some kind of problem on an airplane,
sentences.zh: 所以说到底，如果我真的想在飞机坠毁或遇到某种故障时活下来，

sentences.en: the final step really rests with me.
sentences.zh: 最后一步其实还是取决于我自己。

sentences.en: I have to watch the video.
sentences.zh: 我得看安全视频。

sentences.en: I have to read the card.
sentences.zh: 我得读安全须知卡。

sentences.en: This is my responsibility is to take that final step.
sentences.zh: 我的责任就是迈出这最后一步。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And oh my God, I'm just cringing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我都起鸡皮疙瘩了。

sentences.en: I feel like at the risk of turning this whole story into a PSA, it really is the truth that we all have to actively participate in taking our own safety seriously.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，冒着把整个故事变成公益广告的风险说一句，这确实是事实：我们所有人都必须积极参与，认真对待自身的安全。

sentences.en: And I still, I love the cards.
sentences.zh: 而且我依然，我还是很喜欢那些卡片。

sentences.en: I just see them a little bit differently now.
sentences.zh: 只是现在我看它们的眼光有些不同了。

sentences.en: Before doing all this reporting, to me, they were just like physical laminated artifacts of people pretending to have control in a crisis.
sentences.zh: 在做所有这些报道之前，在我看来，它们不过是人们在危机中假装自己能掌控局面的实体塑封工艺品。

sentences.en: Like, like they were endearing, you know, because they were so futile, because they didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 就好像，就好像它们很可爱，你知道的，因为它们那么徒劳，因为它们根本无足轻重。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's like the main reason that I took them from flights.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我从航班上顺走它们的主要原因。

sentences.en: But now, and I know I'm going to sound like a goody two-shoes saying this, but the next time I board a plane,
sentences.zh: 但现在，我知道我说这话听起来像个老古板，但下次我登上一架飞机时，

sentences.en: I'm going to pull out the safety information card and I'm going to read it, note where the exits are, how to open the door.
sentences.zh: 我会抽出安全信息卡并仔细阅读，记下安全门的位置以及如何打开机门。

sentences.en: And then when I'm finished, I'm going to put it back in the seat back pocket and hope that the next person reads it too.
sentences.zh: 然后当我看完后，我会把它放回座椅背后的口袋里，并希望下一个乘客也能读一读。

sentences.en: When we come back, we'll talk to some of the people who actually draw safety cards for a living and find out why you really want them to do a good job after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将和一些以画安全卡为生的人聊聊，并在之后了解为什么你真的希望他们能把工作做好。

sentences.en: So we're back with safety card criminal, Mo Laborde.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，这位是安全卡“罪犯”莫·拉博德。

sentences.en: So, Mo, I know that there was some stuff that we couldn't fit in the piece and you talked to other people besides Bo and Dan.
sentences.zh: 那么，莫，我知道有些内容我们没能塞进节目里，而且除了博和丹，你还采访了其他人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: When I was researching this story, one of the things I learned is that Bo and Dan had all these great innovations, but, you know, neither of them were artists.
sentences.zh: 我在做这个故事的调研时，了解到的其中一件事就是，博和丹有很多绝妙的创新，但是，你知道的，他们俩都不是艺术家。

sentences.en: Like, they don't draw the cards.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，卡片不是他们画的。

sentences.en: So I got really curious about who it is that does the drawing.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对到底是谁在负责画画这事儿感到好奇。

sentences.en: Like, what actually goes into creating one of these things.
sentences.zh: 比如，制作这些东西到底需要经历什么。

sentences.en: So I called up Brock Fisher and Larry Bruns.
sentences.zh: 于是我打电话联系了布洛克·费舍尔和拉里·布伦斯。

sentences.en: When you tell people this is what you do, what do most people say?
sentences.zh: 当你告诉别人这就是你的工作时，大多数人都会说什么？

sentences.en: One I get a lot of, that's a real job or that pays the bills.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到的一句是，“这也是份真正的工作啊”或者“这还能糊口呢”。

sentences.en: I get that one quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我挺常听到这句的。

sentences.en: Most people don't say anything.
sentences.zh: 大多数人其实什么也没说。

sentences.en: So the first guy you heard is Brock and the second guy is Larry.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才听到的第一个人是布洛克，第二个人是拉里。

sentences.en: Together they comprise Air Safety Art International.
sentences.zh: 他们两个共同组成了国际航空安全艺术公司。

sentences.en: And, adorably, they are a grandfather-grandson safety card design duo.
sentences.zh: 而且，非常可爱的是，他们是一个祖孙档的安全卡设计组合。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And apparently, major airline companies have their own in-house design teaMs.
sentences.zh: 而且显然，各大航空公司都有自己的内部设计团队。

sentences.en: But smaller airlines turn to companies like Brock and Larry's to make their safety cards.
sentences.zh: 但小型航空公司会求助于像布洛克和拉里这样的公司来制作安全卡。

sentences.en: And they also do a lot of private jets and helicopters, which means that they have a lot of fancy clients,
sentences.zh: 他们还承接许多私人飞机和直升机的业务，这意味着他们有很多高档客户，

sentences.en: some of which they could tell me on the record and some of which they couldn't.
sentences.zh: 其中有些他们可以大方透露，有些则不能。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: I can tell you.
sentences.zh: 这个我可以告诉你们。

sentences.en: I did Taylor Swift's Falcon jet.
sentences.zh: 我做过泰勒·斯威夫特的猎鹰喷气式飞机。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if it's the same one she has now, but I did one of Taylor Swift's briefing cards.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是她现在用的那一架，但我确实做过泰勒·斯威夫特的一份安全须知卡。

sentences.en: Yes, I confess I was starstruck.
sentences.zh: 是的，我承认我当时被大明星震撼到了。

sentences.en: I was very impressed.
sentences.zh: 我印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: But even more impressive is that Larry is the guy who did all the drawings for Bo and Dan's first visual cards back in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 但更厉害的是，拉里就是当年在 60 年代为博和丹的第一批视觉化卡片绘制所有插图的那个人。

sentences.en: And, turns out, he's Bo's brother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 而且结果证明，他还是博的连襟。

sentences.en: Oh, so this is like a family, family business.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这是一个彻头彻尾的家族企业。

sentences.en: Totally, yes.
sentences.zh: 完全是，没错。

sentences.en: Which means that Larry helped develop the classic safety card look.
sentences.zh: 这意味着拉里协助奠定了经典安全卡的视觉风格。

sentences.en: The retro clothes and the crisp, clean lines.
sentences.zh: 复古的服装以及利落干净的线条。

sentences.en: And, of course, no words.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有没有文字。

sentences.en: Words in a briefing card just kill me.
sentences.zh: 安全须知卡里出现文字简直要了我的命。

sentences.en: And, unfortunately, they're out there.
sentences.zh: 而且不幸的是，这种卡片外面还挺多。

sentences.en: And for the past few years, he's been teaching his grandson, Brock, all the secrets of safety card illustration.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，他一直把安全卡插画的所有秘诀传授给他的孙子布洛克。

sentences.en: Oh, so, okay, we have to hear some secrets of safety card illustrations.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以，好吧，我们一定要听听安全卡插画的一些秘诀。

sentences.en: What are they?
sentences.zh: 都是些什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what goes into designing a safety card that maybe I am not noticing?
sentences.zh: 我是说，设计一张安全卡有什么是我可能没有注意到的细节吗？

sentences.en: Well, the big goal is that grasping the information presented in the card should feel effortless.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的目标是，理解卡片上呈现的信息应该感觉毫不费力。

sentences.en: So it's trying to make sure that it's a little story and that the whole story makes sense without someone going, whoa, whoa, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以这就得确保它是一个小故事，并且整个故事能让人一看就懂，而不会让人觉得“等等，等一下，什么情况”。

sentences.en: And that little story is the story of how you get off the plane.
sentences.zh: 而那个小故事就是关于你如何离开飞机的故事。

sentences.en: And it starts with making sure you understand where you are in the cabin.
sentences.zh: 它从确保你明白自己身处客舱的什么位置开始。

sentences.en: That's one that kind of gets me when I'm on an airliner is if I'm looking at the card and I look up, do I see the same thing?
sentences.zh: 我在坐民航客机时经常遇到这种情况，如果我看着卡片然后抬头，我看到的是不是跟上面一样的东西？

sentences.en: And then they need to make sure that each scene in the narrative has only like a few key details that stand out.
sentences.zh: 然后他们需要确保叙事中的每个场景只有几个突出的关键细节。

sentences.en: Things like if in that aircraft, that handle is bright red, we need to show it bright red, not a generic gray or black.
sentences.zh: 比如在那架飞机上，那个把手是亮红色的，我们就得把它画成亮红色，而不是通用的灰色或黑色。

sentences.en: It needs to be red because if that's the only thing you remember, at least you know what you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 它必须是红色的，因为如果那是你唯一记住的东西，至少你知道自己在找什么。

sentences.en: So the premise is if I'm panicking, I just have this glowing red handle in my mind's eye from the card.
sentences.zh: 所以前提是，如果我在恐慌中，脑海里只会浮现出卡片上那个发光的红色把手。

sentences.en: And I'm just thinking red handle, red handle.
sentences.zh: 我满脑子都在想红把手、红把手。

sentences.en: And then when I see it, I'm like, success, then next step.
sentences.zh: 然后当我看到它时，我就会想：太棒了，进行下一步。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But even conveying that is a lot of work because all the details you see in the card have to exactly match what's actually in the aircraft so that the passengers don't get confused.
sentences.zh: 但即使要传达这一点也需要大量的工作，因为你在卡片上看到的所有细节都必须与飞机上的实际情况完全吻合，这样乘客才不会感到困惑。

sentences.en: So Larry and Brock told me that they need images or samples of all of the objects in each carrier's version of each different plane.
sentences.zh: 所以拉里和布洛克告诉我，他们需要每个航空公司针对不同机型中所有物品的图片或样品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like, you would be shocked at how many different types of door handles there are or safety vests there are.
sentences.zh: 比如，你会对市面上门把手或救生衣的种类繁多感到震惊。

sentences.en: There are so many types of inflatable safety vests.
sentences.zh: 充气救生衣的类型实在是太多了。

sentences.en: Larry and Brock say they've drawn about 150 types of life vests and rafts.
sentences.zh: 拉里和布洛克说他们大约画过 150 种救生衣和救生筏。

sentences.en: I had never really thought of that, but that's totally true.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未想过这一点，但这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that has to be exactly right or it doesn't really do its job.
sentences.zh: 对，这些必须完全正确，否则就无法发挥作用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the same thing goes for all the different actions that the passengers are expected to perform.
sentences.zh: 乘客被期望执行的所有不同动作也是如此。

sentences.en: Because they need to accurately convey what each of those actions look like, but also feel like.
sentences.zh: 因为他们需要准确传达每一个动作看起来是什么样的，甚至感觉是什么样的。

sentences.en: When we draw people, we have them carry weight.
sentences.zh: 当我们画人的时候，我们会让他们表现出负重感。

sentences.en: Like, we add muscle shape inside the lines.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们在线条内部加入肌肉的轮廓。

sentences.en: We kind of, like, show them bending and the creakles in the shirt so it looks like he's heaving this raft.
sentences.zh: 我们会在某种程度上画出他们的弯曲姿势以及衬衫上的褶皱，好让看起来他正在吃力地搬运这个救生筏。

sentences.en: So we create the illusion of mass and weight really quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能非常迅速地营造出体量感和重量感的错觉。

sentences.en: And that means that they've also ended up with a vast library of customized character poses.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们最终也积累了大量的定制角色姿势库。

sentences.en: So in the end, we probably have, I don't know, we've never done the math.
sentences.zh: 所以到最后，我们大概有，我不知道，我们从没算过。

sentences.en: There's got to be a thousand different characters.
sentences.zh: 怎么也得有一千个不同的角色吧。

sentences.en: And 985 of them are me.
sentences.zh: 其中 985 个都是我。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is the final safety card secret.
sentences.zh: 这是安全卡的终极秘诀。

sentences.en: Many of the characters you see in their cards, regardless of what they look like on the page, really, they're just Brock.
sentences.zh: 你在他们的卡片上看到的许多角色，无论他们在纸面上看起来如何，其实，他们都只是布洛克。

sentences.en: Like, they're just based on photos of him in a nice pair of slacks and a dress shirt.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们只是以他穿着得体的休闲裤和正装衬衫的照片为基础创作的。

sentences.en: People actually, like, wise up to that.
sentences.zh: 人们其实会慢慢察觉到这一点。

sentences.en: They'll start to look and be like, it's just the same guy in every situation on this card.
sentences.zh: 他们会开始端详然后心想：这张卡片上每种情况里的不都是同一个人吗。

sentences.en: That's so good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: This is my favorite fun fact, because when Brock's body type won't do, they just recruit anybody, like their cousin, their spouse, their friend, to come put on business casual or,
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的趣闻，因为当布洛克的体型不适合时，他们就会招募任何人，比如他们的表亲、配偶、朋友来换上商务休闲装，或者，

sentences.en: like, a flight attendant outfit and pose for the cards.
sentences.zh: 比如空乘制服，然后为卡片摆好姿势。

sentences.en: We, for some reason, recruit waitresses from restaurants that we used to go to when we were in Bellingham.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，我们会去招募以前在贝灵厄姆时经常去的餐馆的服务员。

sentences.en: We ask them if they want to make an extra hundred bucks.
sentences.zh: 我们问他们想不想多赚一百块钱。

sentences.en: And they usually say yes.
sentences.zh: 他们通常都会答应。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Just come over to my house and pretend to be a crash card model?
sentences.zh: 直接来我家然后假装扮演安全卡模特？

sentences.en: Yeah, and they actually asked me if I wanted to be a safety card model.
sentences.zh: 对，而且他们甚至还问过我想不想当安全卡模特。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Did you say yes?
sentences.zh: 你答应了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I was like.
sentences.zh: 答应了，我当时心想。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然要。

sentences.en: It is super niche and super cool.
sentences.zh: 这超级小众又超级酷。

sentences.en: They haven't had an order come in where they need basically a woman to do a very specific action yet.
sentences.zh: 他们目前还没接到需要女性来完成某个非常特定动作的订单。

sentences.en: But when they do, I'll be there.
sentences.zh: 但只要订单一来，我就会上场。

sentences.en: Mo, this has been so much fun.
sentences.zh: 莫，这期节目太有趣了。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: It's a huge help to us when you review it in lots of different places.
sentences.zh: 你在很多不同的地方写书评对我们来说是巨大的帮助。
